title: Sequential Spinodal Decompositions and Ordering Reactions in an As-Quenched Cr<sub>39</sub>Co<sub>18</sub>Fe<sub>18</sub>Ni<sub>18</sub>Al<sub>7</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: An arc-melted, homogenized high-entropy alloy of nominal composition Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 (at. %).
recollection.intervention: As-quenched from the homogenization temperature (~1200 °C) into water, followed by isothermal aging at 600–800 °C for times up to 100 h.
recollection.structure: Initially single-phase body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solution; then a fine, compositionally modulated spinodal microstructure (lamellar Cr-rich and NiCo-rich BCC regions) develops, and the NiCo-rich regions subsequently order to a B2 (ordered BCC) phase.
recollection.mechanism: Sequential spinodal decomposition within the supersaturated BCC matrix driven by uphill diffusion of Cr vs. Ni/Co, creating composition waves; these Ni/Co-enriched waves undergo an ordering reaction to form the B2 structure.
recollection.results: Onset of detectable spinodal modulation after ~1 h at 600 °C, with a modulation wavelength of ~8 nm and ~10 at.% compositional amplitude; by 10 h at 700 °C, ~40 % of the volume had transformed to the ordered B2 phase (ordering parameter S ≈0.6), raising hardness from ~200 HV in the as-quenched state to ~400 HV.

score.note: The annealing intervention is incorrect: the paper used brief anneals at 1100–1300 °C followed by water quenching, not aging at 600–800 °C. The recollection correctly invokes BCC spinodal separation and subsequent B2 ordering, but misses the reciprocal hierarchical BCC/B2 structure and incorrectly attributes enrichment/order primarily to Ni–Co rather than Ni–Al. All reported aging times, wavelengths, phase fractions, ordering parameters, and hardness values are unsupported and conflict with the actual HRC results and particle sizes.
